location_detail: Lhende Khola into the Bhote Koshi, near the Nepal–Tibet border
downstream_note: The Rasuwa Bhote Koshi becomes the Trishuli, then the Narayani, then the Gandak, which crosses into Bihar. NOT the Koshi: two different Nepali rivers are called the Bhote Koshi, and only the Sindhupalchok one feeds the Saptakoshi. The sources point the same way: a rescue from the Trishuli tunnel, a body recovered in the Narayani, supplied imagery of Manakamana, which sits above the Trishuli in Gorkha. Assam and north Bengal are the Brahmaputra and the Teesta, and are not downstream of this event.
mechanism_stated: Ice-rock / glacier collapse, which blocked the river and then released

owner_figures.label: People affected
owner_figures.source_name: IFRC, reported by UN News, 28 August 2026
owner_figures.note: Homes, roads, bridges, hydropower and whole stretches of the valley. The figure is the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies'; David Fisher, its head of delegation in Nepal, gave it, and UN News carried it beside UN OCHA's toll on 28 August. Some outlets frame the same number as Nepal and Tibet together.

owner_figures.label: Children affected
owner_figures.note: UNICEF's own press release: "At least 17,000 children have been impacted by the devastating flash floods that tore through Nepal's Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts on 26 August." Alice Akunga, UNICEF Representative to Nepal. Its title renders the same count as children in need of urgent humanitarian assistance; 18 schools were destroyed and 20 damaged.

owner_figures.label: Households needing shelter
owner_figures.note: "More than 10,000 households along the Trishuli corridor need emergency shelter and relief supplies." A count of households in need, not of homes destroyed. One resettled community of 250 households on the low banks of the Trishuli — rebuilt there after the 2015 earthquake — was swept away entirely, per CARE Nepal's country director Mona Sherpa.
